title: MergeRequestReviewReport
description: Output for the `merge-request` agent in branch-review form. The core review sections (acceptance_criteria, adr_review, findings, verdict) apply in both modes; recommended_comments is for peer mode and pr_summary for self mode. Leave inapplicable sections empty/omitted. human_summary is always last.

mode.description: Which review mode ran: peer = review someone else's branch; self = review your own branch and write the merge-request description.

walkthrough.description: A 2-4 sentence plain-English summary of what the change does, judged against the commit messages (and the stated intent when provided). No findings -- just the 'what' and 'why'.

acceptance_criteria.description: The requirements review: does the diff satisfy the acceptance criteria? When none were given, leave criteria and scope_drift empty and say so in summary/notes -- never invent criteria.

source.description: Where the criteria came from (the input text, a pasted ticket), or empty when none were provided.

criteria.description: One entry per acceptance criterion, judged against the diff. Empty when none were provided.

criterion.description: The criterion, quoted or closely paraphrased from the input.

status.description: met = fully satisfied with evidence; partially_met = a gap remains; not_met = not satisfied or no implementing change; not_verifiable = can't be judged from the diff alone.

evidence.description: The concrete diff evidence, or 'no implementing change found in the diff' for an unimplemented not_met.

gap.description: For partially_met/not_met: what is missing and what it would take. Omit/'None' for met.

scope_drift.description: Changes that map to NO acceptance criterion. Empty when all trace to a criterion or none were provided.

summary.description: The overall requirements verdict in one or two lines.

notes.description: Brief meta-note about where the criteria came from, or that none were given.

adr_review.description: The architecture-compliance review against the team's ADRs, retrieved from a knowledge collection.

adrs_consulted.description: Sources/identifiers of the ADRs retrieved. Empty when no ADR collection was reachable.

compliance.description: One entry per governing ADR the diff touches. Records violations and deliberate compliance.

suggested_fix.description: For a violation/at_risk: a concrete fix. Omit/'No action needed' for complies.

adr_reference.description: The ADR this entry is grounded in. Every entry must cite a retrieved ADR.

rule.description: The rule, quoted or closely paraphrased from the retrieved chunk.

notes.description: Brief meta-note about the ADR check itself.

architecture_concerns.description: Architectural drift the ADRs do not yet name. Not ADR violations. Empty when none.

other_findings.description: Non-architecture findings a competent reviewer would raise -- correctness, security, tests. A blocker is still a blocker. Empty when none.

praiseworthy.description: What the change genuinely does well. Specific, honest; leave empty rather than padding.

needs_attention.description: A prioritized digest of the few highest-impact things to address first, each drawn from a detailed finding above and pointing back to it. A synthesis -- NOT new findings. Empty when clean.

source.description: Which section this item is drawn from.

verdict.description: approve = satisfies the criteria (when given), complies with governing ADRs, and is clean -- peer: mergeable; self: ready to open. approve_with_nits = only minor/optional items remain. request_changes = at least one blocking item -- an unmet required criterion, a blocker/high ADR violation, or a blocking correctness/security finding.

verdict_rationale.description: One line explaining the verdict, framed for the mode -- e.g. (peer) 'AC-3 unimplemented; violates the Data Layer ADR', (self) 'All criteria met; ready to open'.

recommended_comments.description: peer mode: the review comments to leave on the pull request -- each a finished, second-person, paste-ready comment (not a summary of one), covering the needs_attention items and warranted praise. Empty only when there is genuinely nothing to say.

comment.description: The comment body exactly as it should appear on the pull request.

pr_summary.description: self mode only: the merge-request write-up composed from the diff. The human_summary renders this as the paste-ready description. Omit in peer mode.

summary.description: What this branch changes and WHY, grounded in the diff/commits (and the stated intent when present).

changes.description: The change set grouped by area/purpose.

highlights.description: The few things a reviewer should look at most closely. Empty when straightforward.

testing.description: How the change was verified and/or how a reviewer can verify it. 'Not yet tested' is honest if so.

human_summary.description: Written LAST and placed at the very end. Rendered for the active mode: peer -> a plain-English 'Bottom Line' (does it satisfy the criteria/ADRs, what most needs attention, the action); self -> the paste-ready merge-request description assembled from pr_summary (title, summary, grouped files-changed, highlights, testing) in Markdown. Two to four sentences unless it is the self-mode description.
